sections.content: How many people are "human resources and industrial relations officers"?

156,730 people

were counted on the census as "human resources and industrial relations officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Human resources and industrial relations officers conduct research, analyse data and advise on recruitment, training, staff appraisal and industrial relations policies, and assist specialist managers with negotiations on behalf of a commercial enterprise, trade union or other organisation.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "human resources and industrial relations officers", 21.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "human resources and industrial relations officers" was 16 to 19 years.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "human resources and industrial relations officers" there were more women than men (69.8% compared with 30.2%).

This means "human resources and industrial relations officers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 30.2% and women made up 69.8% of "human resources and industrial relations officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "human resources and industrial relations officers" included:

  • dispensing opticians
  • housing officers
  • coffee shop workers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "human resources and industrial relations officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "human resources and industrial relations officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "human resources and industrial relations officers", 8.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82.4% compared with 17.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.1%) than self-employed (4.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
